title: Another planetary warfare game (Ain't Astra a wonder)
author: affabledrunk
selftext:
**Stones from Heaven : Orbital Warfare**

[Github](https://github.com/xbenevolence131/sfhow.git)

I mostly made this as an experiment. Sharing the game and my wonder here.

Someone posted their (superior!) orbital mechanics game, which got me thinking about ideas I’d had over the years, so I gave it a go.

I use AI tools all the time, but I’d always been dubious of the little one-shot game demos. I’d made games with Codex before, but hadn’t tried Astra.

So I rambled at ChatGPT about throwing asteroids at planets and had it turn that into a modest game-design document. I gave that to Codex Astra, and it essentially one-shotted the core gameplay, structure and aesthetics. It even supplied an asteroid belt with the sideways velocities needed to keep the rocks orbiting—without me specifying that.

I spent another afternoon tuning it and adding a tutorial, but the bones were there from the first generation. Boosters rendezvous with asteroids and push them towards enemy planets; platforms, drones and combat ships handle defence and interception. Minimalist visuals, predicted trajectories, and time to think.

For bonus points, I tried voice mode while playtesting, and that fucking blew my mind too. Playing, talking through changes, then trying them out—all while drinking Miller Lite and watching Star Trek reruns.

Amazing time to be alive.

comments.author: jtabernik
comments.body: This looks cool!  Thanks for sharing!
